source_text: δευτέρᾳ παρουσίᾳ ἰδεῖν περιμενόμενον. τοῦτο γὰρ σημαίνει τό τε: «ἐν πνεύματι διὰ χειλέων ἀνελεῖ ἀσεβεῖς», καὶ τὸ ἀλλαχοῦ εἰρημένον τῷ αὐτῷ προφήτῃ· «ἐν πνεύματι κρίσεως καὶ ἐν πνεύματι καύσεως.» ∆αυὶδ δὲ ἐν ρληʹ ψαλμῷ φησιν· «ποῦ πορευθῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός σου; καὶ ἀπὸ προσώπου σου ποῦ φύγω»; τό· «ποῦ πορευθῶ» καὶ «ποῦ φύγω» πλατεῖαν ἔχει ἔμφασιν· σημαίνει γὰρ πανταχοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κριτὴν ὑπάρχειν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα. «φοβερόν», γὰρ ὡς ἀληθῶς, κατὰ τὸν ἀπόστολον, «ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖ ρας θεοῦ ζῶντος», τοῦ λέγοντος, ἐν μθʹ ψαλμῷ· «ἐλέγξω καὶ παραστήσω κατὰ πρόσωπόν σου τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου.» καὶ τοῦ Μιχαίου δὲ ἡ μικρῷ πρόσθεν λεχθεῖσα προφητεία καὶ εἰς τόδε συντελεῖ τὸ κεφάλαιον. ποίαν δὲ ἀπόδειξιν ἂν εἴποι τις ἰσχυροτέραν εἰς τοῦτο τοῦ καὶ σωτῆρα παρ' Ἰωάννῃ λέγειν περὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος· «ἐλθὼν ἐκεῖνος ἐλέγξει τὸν κόσμον περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ δικαιο σύνης καὶ περὶ κρίσεως»; 7.10ν ὅτι ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ πνεύματος Ἐλύμαν τὸν μάγον ἐξετύφλωσεν ὅτι ἐν τῇ ὑπερβαλλούσῃ δυνάμει τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ὁ Παῦλος ἐν Κύπρῳ Ἐλύμαν τὸν μάγον, ἐπιστρατεύοντα τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ λυμαινόμενον τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, ἐξετύφλωσεν λόγῳ. τοῦ πνεύματος γὰρ εἶναι τὴν δύναμιν δεικνῦσα ἡ γραφή, λέγει αὐτοῖς ὀνόμασιν οὕτως· «τότε ὁ Παῦλος πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου, εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· ἰδοὺ χεὶρ κυρίου ἐπὶ σὲ καὶ ἔσῃ τυφλὸς μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον.» ἀληθῶς γὰρ οὐκ αὐτόν, μὴ ἔχοντα τοῦ πνεύματος τὴν πάντα ἐνεργοῦσαν δύναμιν, ἀνθρώπου μαγγανείαις σώζοντος καὶ δαίμοσι πεποιθότος τὸ βλέπειν ῥήματι ἀποσβέσαι. 7.11ν ὅτι τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ παναγίου πνεύματος ἀνεῳχθέντες οἱ οὐρανοὶ ὤφθησαν τῷ ὁσίῳ Στεφάνῳ. ὅτι τῇ δυνάμει καὶ χάριτι τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἀναπτυχθέντες οἱ οὐρανοὶ ὤφθησαν τῷ διπλοῦς στεφάνους
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... but him, as judge with the Holy Spirit in the] second coming, awaited to be seen. For this is what is signified both by: 'in spirit through lips he will destroy the ungodly', and by what was said elsewhere by the same prophet: 'in a spirit of judgment and in a spirit of burning.' And David in the 138th psalm (LXX; English 139) says: 'Where shall I go from your Spirit? And from your face where shall I flee?' The 'where shall I go' and 'where shall I flee' has a broad emphasis; for it signifies that the Holy Spirit is present everywhere and is judge. For 'fearful', truly, according to the apostle, 'is it to fall into the hands of the living God,' who says in the 49th psalm (LXX; English 50): 'I will convict and set before your face your sins.' And the prophecy of Micah spoken a little before also contributes to this heading. And what proof stronger for this could one name than the Saviour also saying in John about the Holy Spirit: 'That one, having come, will convict the world about sin and about righteousness and about judgment'? 7.10ν [Chapter title:] That Paul in the power of the Spirit blinded Elymas the sorcerer. That in the surpassing power of the Holy Spirit Paul in Cyprus blinded with a word Elymas the sorcerer, who was campaigning against the saints and outraging the truth. For the Scripture, showing that the power is the Spirit's, says in the very words thus: 'Then Paul, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, said to him: Behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun.' For truly it was not [possible for] him, not having the power of the Spirit that works all things, to quench with a word the seeing of a man keeping himself safe by sorceries and having trusted in demons. 7.11ν [Chapter title:] That by the power of the all-holy Spirit the heavens, having been opened, were seen by the holy Stephen. That by the power and grace of the Holy Spirit the heavens, having been unfolded, were seen by the one [who had bound on] double crowns [continues in the next section] ...
pass_b_english: …second coming he is awaited, to be seen. For this is what is meant both by “with the Spirit, through his lips, he will destroy the ungodly” (Isaiah 11:4) and by the words spoken elsewhere by the same prophet: “by a spirit of judgment and by a spirit of burning” (Isaiah 4:4). And David says in the hundred and thirty-ninth Psalm: “Where shall I go from your Spirit? And where shall I flee from your face?” (Psalm 139:7). The words “where shall I go” and “where shall I flee” carry a broad meaning: they signify that the Holy Spirit is present everywhere and is judge. For truly, as the apostle says, “it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God” (Hebrews 10:31), who says in the fiftieth Psalm, “I will convict you, and set your sins before your face” (Psalm 50:21). The prophecy of Micah quoted a little earlier also bears on this heading (Micah 3:8). And what stronger proof of this could anyone name than that the Saviour himself, in John, says of the Holy Spirit: “When he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment” (John 16:8)?
That Paul, by the power of the Spirit, blinded Elymas the sorcerer.

It was by the surpassing power of the Holy Spirit that Paul, in Cyprus, blinded with a word Elymas the sorcerer, who was making war on the saints and doing violence to the truth. For Scripture, to show that the power was the Spirit’s, says in so many words: “Then Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to him: ‘Look, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun’” (Acts 13:9-11). And truly, had he not had the Spirit’s power that works all things, he could not by a word have quenched the sight of a man who kept himself safe by sorceries and trusted in demons.
That by the power of the all-holy Spirit the heavens were opened and seen by holy Stephen.
It was by the power and grace of the Holy Spirit that the heavens were unfolded and seen by the man with the double crowns…

choices.issue: Chapter titles run into the text (Elymas and Stephen sentences printed twice); wrong Psalm number and wording; references
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u19): retranslated. The old English ran the chapter titles 7.10 and 7.11 into the prose ('For Paul, in the power of the Spirit, blinded the magician Elymas; for in the surpassing power...'), so each thought was printed twice as one paragraph; the titles now stand alone as headings and each body sentence follows as the copy-text has it. It also gave 'Psalm 51' and 'I will confess' for Greek Psalm 49:21 (English 50:21), 'the prophecy of Michael ... mentioned briefly' for Micah's prophecy quoted a little earlier, 'said ... to the same prophet' for the dative of agent, 'ravaging with the truth' for λυμαινόμενον τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, and made nonsense of the last Elymas sentence. References: (Acts 13:11) -> (Acts 13:9-11), since the quotation begins with 'Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit' (13:9); (Heb 10:31) -> (Hebrews 10:31); (Psalm 139:7) and (Micah 3:8) added.

choices.english: …second coming he is awaited, to be seen
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence: the previous section ends κριτὴν δὲ αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι ἐν τῇ ('but as judge together with the Holy Spirit, at the'). Only the words this section holds are translated.
Dative of agent with εἰρημένον; Isaiah is the speaker, not the one addressed.

choices.english: in the hundred and thirty-ninth Psalm
choices.why: Greek Psalm 138 = English 139; the verse quoted is 139:7.
Greek Psalm 49 = English 50; the verse quoted is 50:21. The old English printed 'Psalm 51'.

choices.term: ἡ μικρῷ πρόσθεν λεχθεῖσα προφητεία (of Micah)
choices.english: The prophecy of Micah quoted a little earlier also bears on this heading (Micah 3:8)
choices.why: Didymus refers back to Micah 3:5 and 3:8 ('I will fill strength in the Spirit of the Lord and of judgment'), quoted in u18-rem-early; the judgment of the Spirit is the point, so 3:8 is cited.

choices.english: That Paul, by the power of the Spirit, blinded Elymas the sorcerer. / That by the power of the all-holy Spirit the heavens were opened and seen by holy Stephen.
choices.why: Chapter titles, each its own paragraph. The copy-text opens each chapter by restating its title with a second ὅτι clause in fuller words; that clause is rendered 'It was by ... that ...', so the reader sees title and thesis, not the same sentence twice.
αὐτοῖς ὀνόμασιν, 'in the very words': Scripture names the Holy Spirit explicitly.

choices.english: had he not had the Spirit’s power that works all things, he could not by a word have quenched
choices.why: The infinitive depends on an understood 'it was possible'; μὴ ἔχοντα is conditional.

choices.english: a man who kept himself safe by sorceries
choices.why: σώζοντος has no object in the Greek; 'himself' is understood. 'Saving by human magic' (old English) misread the genitive ἀνθρώπου.

choices.english: the man with the double crowns…
choices.why: The phrase runs into the next section (ἀναδησαμένῳ ἀποστολῆς καὶ μαρτυρίου, 'which he bound on, of apostleship and martyrdom'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'. There is a play on Stephen's name (Στέφανος, 'crown'), which English cannot keep.
